## Mothur v1.48.3 and UNITE v10.0 and clustering in groups of three for stats

```{r}
library(decontam)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
library(grid)
library(reshape2)
library(phyloseq)
library(Polychrome)
library(tidyverse)
library(viridis)
library(emmeans)
library(ggpubr)
```

```{r}
setwd("D:/TEGU_CODE_FILE_MASTER") #working directory 

theme_set(theme_bw())

source("miseqR.R")
# this file is saved in the working directory
```

## Data Import

Now I will import all of the mothur data along with the metadata file:

```{r}
# Assign variables for imported data
sharedfile = "TEGUITS2.shared"
taxfile = "TEGUITS2.taxonomy"
mapfile = "Tegu_FinalMetadata.csv"

# Import mothur data
mothur_ITS2 <- import_mothur(mothur_shared_file = sharedfile,
  mothur_constaxonomy_file = taxfile)

# Import sample metadata
map <- read.csv(mapfile)
```

Convert the metadata dataframe into phyloseq format with a simple constructor. The only formatting required to merge the sample data into a phyloseq object is that the row names must match the sample names in your shared and taxonomy files.

```{r}
map <- sample_data(map)

# Assign rownames to be Sample names 
rownames(map) <- map$SampleName

# Merge mothurdata object with sample metadata
ITS_merge <- merge_phyloseq(mothur_ITS2, map)
ITS_merge
```

```{r}
colnames(tax_table(ITS_merge)) #these names are not helpful

#change column names 
colnames(tax_table(ITS_merge)) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", 
  "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species") #unlik 16S, I was able to get some species level resolution 
```

## Decontam

Using the decontam package to remove any contamination that was introduced during the extraction and PCR process. Lets look at the library size:

```{r}
df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(ITS_merge)) # Put sample_data into a ggplot-friendly data.frame
df$LibrarySize <- sample_sums(ITS_merge)
df <- df[order(df$LibrarySize),]
df$Index <- seq(nrow(df))
ggplot(data=df, aes(x=Index, y=LibrarySize, color=SampleORControl)) + geom_point()
```

It looks like we were unable to get any good sequencing from the blanks, regardless if they were extraction or PCR blanks. They got removed in the trimming processes in Mothur, meaning we must proceed with a frequency method.

```{r}
#frequency default threshold 0.1 
contamdf.freq <- isContaminant(ITS_merge, method="frequency", conc="DNAQuant")
head(contamdf.freq)
```

We can see whether or not a sequence statistically deviates from the set threshold looking at the \$contaminant column.

```{r}
table(contamdf.freq$contaminant)
```

Out of the total 15,948 sequences, 182 have been identified as potential contaminants.

```{r}
fung.noncontam <- prune_taxa(!contamdf.freq$contaminant, ITS_merge)
fung.noncontam
```

I now have 15,948 sequences to work with.

## Graphical Analyses

#### Sample Summary:

Looking at the distribution of the read counts from the samples, this is very similar to what we did earlier before we performed our decontam:

```{r}
summary_df <- as.data.frame(sample_data(fung.noncontam)) #create a new data frame 
summary_df$LibrarySize <- sample_sums(fung.noncontam)
summary_df <- summary_df[order(summary_df$LibrarySize),]
summary_df$Index <- seq(nrow(summary_df))

png("LibrarySizeTeguITS.png", width = 800, height = 600)
ggplot(data=summary_df, aes(x=Index, y=LibrarySize, color=Location)) + geom_point()
dev.off()
```

So, similar to the 16S rRNA data, we see that the swabs have the lowest read counts and that the control soil and tegu decomposition impacted soils are similar to each other in read counts.

```{r}
#min, max, and mean of the sample read counts 
smin <- min(sample_sums(fung.noncontam))
smean <- mean(sample_sums(fung.noncontam))
smax <- max(sample_sums(fung.noncontam))
total_dataset_reads <- sum(sample_sums(fung.noncontam))
```

The minimum read count is 822 sequences, the maximum is 499,570 and the mean is \~149,407.

#### Stacked Barplots:

Reduce the phyla to remove OTUs with \>2% relative abundance.

```{r}
tegits_phylum2 <- fung.noncontam %>%
  tax_glom(taxrank = "Phylum") %>%  
  transform_sample_counts(function(x) {x/sum(x)} ) %>%  
  psmelt() %>% 
   filter(Abundance > 0.02) %>%    # Filter out low abundance taxa
  arrange(Phylum)
```

```{r}
#filtering into treatment groups

FCon <-filter(tegits_phylum2,Location == "Control")
FDecomp <-filter(tegits_phylum2,Location == "Tegu")
FSwab <- filter(tegits_phylum2,Location == "Swab")
FBlank <-filter(tegits_phylum2, Location == "Blank")
```

```{r}
tegits_phylum2$Phylum <-as.factor(tegits_phylum2$Phylum)
levels(tegits_phylum2$Phylum)
```

```{r}
#making color pallete 
set.seed(123)
P10 <- createPalette(10, c("#FF0000", "#00FF00", "#0000FF"), range = c(30, 80))

#we are then gonna sort by hue and make a matrix 
P10 <- sortByHue(P10)
P10 <- as.vector(t(matrix(P10, ncol=4)))
swatch(P10)

names(P10) <- levels(c(tegits_phylum2$Phylum))
```

```{r}
FCon <- subset(FCon, Stage != 'Void ')
FCon$Stage <- factor(FCon$Stage, levels = c("Early", "Bloat", "Active I", "Active II", "Active III ", "Advanced I", "Advanced II", "Advanced III", "Skeletal I ", "Skeletal II"))
pdf("ConPhylaTeguITS.pdf", width = 10, height = 7)
ggplot(FCon, aes(x = Stage, 
                         y = Abundance/3, 
                         fill = Phylum)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = P10) +
   theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust=1, size = 14), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16), plot.title = element_text(size = 20))+
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = FALSE, 
                             keywidth = 1.5, 
                             keyheight = 1.5,
                             ncol = 1,
                            legend.text = element_text(size=14))) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  ylab("Relative Abundance (>2%)") +
  xlab ("Decomposition Stage") 
dev.off()
```

Looking at the specific classes by percent relative abundance

```{r}
relabun.class.its <- transform_sample_counts(fung.noncontam,function(x) x / sum(x))
its_class <- tax_glom(relabun.class.its, taxrank = "Class", NArm = FALSE)
class_sub_its <- subset_taxa(its_class, Class %in% c("c__Sordariomycetes","c__Tremellomycetes","c__Saccharomycetes"))
class_its.df <- psmelt(class_sub_its)
head(class_its.df)
```

```{r}
Class_Summary_ITS <- class_its.df %>%
  group_by(Location, Stage, Class) %>%
  summarize(mean_abund = mean(Abundance, na.rm=TRUE)) 
head(Class_Summary_ITS)
```

```{r}
ConClassITS <-filter(Class_Summary_ITS,Location == "Control")
DecompClassITS <-filter(Class_Summary_ITS,Location == "Tegu")
SwabClassITS <- filter(Class_Summary_ITS,Location == "Swab")
Sordario <- filter(Class_Summary_ITS,Class == "c__Sordariomycetes")
Tremello <- filter(Class_Summary_ITS,Class == "c__Tremellomycetes")
```

```{r}
Sord.mod <- aov(mean_abund~factor(Location)+Error(factor(Stage)), data = Sordario)
summary(Sord.mod)  
#There is a significant difference in the mean relative abundance of sordariomycetes across sample types (p=0.0011)

Sord.emm <- emmeans(Sord.mod, ~ Location)
pairs(Sord.emm)
#these significant differences are between the control soils and swabs (p=0.0169) and control and tegu (p=0.0010), not between swabs and decomp 
```

```{r}
Trem.mod <- aov(mean_abund~factor(Location)+Error(factor(Stage)), data = Tremello)
summary(Trem.mod)  
#There is a significant difference in the mean relative abundance of tremellomycetes across sample types (p=0.0369)

Trem.emm <- emmeans(Trem.mod, ~ Location)
pairs(Trem.emm)
#these significant differences are between the control soils and swabs (p=0.0425), not between swabs and decomp 
```

#### Ordination (Unconstrained):

First lets try a PCA:

```{r}
allits <- subset_samples(fung.noncontam, Stage != 'Void ') #this will have everything sans the blanks and removed sample

allits_scale <- allits %>%
  scale_reads(round = "round") #this is from the miseqR.R file

#comparing sample types from different decomposition stages
sample_data(allits_scale)$Stage <- factor(
  sample_data(allits_scale)$Stage, 
  levels = c("Early", "Bloat", "Active I", "Active II", "Active III ", "Advanced I", "Advanced II", "Advanced III", "Skeletal I ", "Skeletal II"))

#ordinnate the data 
allits_pcoa <- ordinate(
  physeq = allits_scale, 
 method = "PCoA", 
  distance = "bray"
)
```

```{r}
#This is exploratory to see if there is any clusering of sample types 
plot_ordination(
  physeq = allits_scale,
  ordination = allits_pcoa,
  shape = "Location",
  color = "Stage",
  title = "PCoA of Fungal Communities") + 
  labs(shape = "Location") +
  scale_color_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "C")+
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Stage), 
             alpha = 0.7, 
             size = 5) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey90", 
             size = 1.5)+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12), axis.title.x = element_text(size=14), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14), plot.title = element_text(size = 20))
```

Distinct clustering based on the sample type.

Now I want to just subset the soil:

```{r}
soilfung <- subset_samples(fung.noncontam, Source == 'Soil ')
soilfung2 <- subset_samples(soilfung, Stage != 'Void ')
#scale to even read depth 
soilits_scale <- soilfung2 %>%
  scale_reads(round = "round") #this is from the miseqR.R file

#comparing sample types from different decomposition stages
sample_data(soilits_scale)$Stage <- factor(
  sample_data(soilits_scale)$Stage, 
  levels = c("Early", "Bloat", "Active I", "Active II", "Active III ", "Advanced I", "Advanced II", "Advanced III", "Skeletal I ", "Skeletal II"))

#ordinnate the data 
soilits_pcoa <- ordinate(
  physeq = soilits_scale, 
 method = "PCoA", 
  distance = "bray"
)
```

Now do biplot with the chemical data overlaying:

```{r}
# Create the distance matrix
soilits_dist <-phyloseq::distance(physeq = soilits_scale, method = "bray")

# Create the CAP ordination
soilits_cap_ord <- ordinate(
  physeq = soilits_scale,
  method = "CAP",
  distance = soilits_dist,
  formula = ~ pH + EC + NH4 + NO3 + C + N + CtoN)

pdf("CAPTEGUITSPoster.pdf", width=9, height=6, useDingbats=FALSE)
soilitscap_plot <- plot_ordination(
  physeq = soilits_scale, 
  ordination = soilits_cap_ord,
  color = "Stage",
  shape = "Location") + 
  theme_classic() +
     labs(shape = 'Treatment') +
  scale_color_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "C")+
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Stage), alpha = 0.7, size = 6) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("Tegu" = 15, "Control" = 16)) +
 # geom_point(colour = "grey90", size = 1.5) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 18), axis.title.x = element_text(size=20), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 18),axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20), plot.title = element_text(size = 24))
  
# add metadata as arrows
Soilits_arrows <- vegan::scores(soilits_cap_ord, display = "bp")

#add labels and create dataframe
Soilits_arrows_df <- data.frame(labels = rownames(Soilits_arrows), Soilits_arrows)

# create arrow aesthetics
ar_aesthetics <- aes(xend = CAP1, yend = CAP2, x = 0, y = 0, shape = NULL, color = NULL, label = labels)
lb_aesthetics <- aes (x = 1.2 * CAP1, y = 1.5 * CAP2, shape = NULL, color = NULL, label = labels)
ar_head = arrow(length = unit (0.02, "npc"))

# overlay arrows
soilitscap_plot+
```

**PERMANOVA:**

Testing the hypothesis that the three different sample locations (Control soils, Tegu decomp soils, and skin swabs) have different centroids.

```{r}
set.seed(3)

# Calculate bray curtis distance matrix with all_scale because it has all samples sans the blank 
allits_bray <- phyloseq::distance(allits_scale, method = "bray") 

# make a data frame from the sample_data and have to use all which is the data with blank removed
allitsdf <- data.frame(sample_data(allits))

# Adonis test
adonis(allits_bray ~ Location, data = allitsdf)

# Homogeneity of dispersion test
betaits_all <- betadisper(allits_bray, allitsdf$Location)
permutest(betaits_all)
```

It looks like there is a differences in community centroids based on sampling location. However, I want to do this for just the soil as well.

```{r}
set.seed(3)

# Calculate bray curtis distance matrix with soil_scale because it has only the soil samples
soilits_bray <- phyloseq::distance(soilits_scale, method = "bray") 

# make a data frame from the sample_data and have to use which is the data with just soils 
soilitsdf <- data.frame(sample_data(soilfung2))

# Adonis test
adonis(soilits_bray ~ Location, data = soilitsdf)

# Homogeneity of dispersion test
betaitssoil <- betadisper(soilits_bray, soilitsdf$Location)
permutest(betaitssoil)
```

And there is still a significant difference in between the soil communities.

#### Alpha Diversity:

First, I must perform rarefaction, although rarefaction has its issues, this needs to be done for these metrics.

```{r}
min_ITS_lib <- min(sample_sums(allits))
#the minimum library is 822 with all samples

min_ITS_lib2 <- min(sample_sums(soilfung2))
#if we don't include the swabs, this makes it so the min library size is 17,289

#I also want to seperate out just the swabs 
skinfung <- subset_samples(fung.noncontam, Source == 'Skin')
skinfung2 <- subset_samples(skinfung, Stage != 'Void ')

min_lib3 <- min(sample_sums(skinfung2))
#okay, so same as min library one, 822, which means swabs must be processed seperately 
```

```{r}
#to make the rarefaction curve, need to extract otu table 
taxa_are_rows(fung.noncontam)

OTUtabITS <- otu_table(fung.noncontam)
class(OTUtabITS) <- "matrix" # as.matrix() will do nothing
## you get a warning here, but this is what we need to have
OTUtabITS <- t(OTUtabITS) # transpose observations to rows
```

```{r}
rareITS <- rarecurve(OTUtabITS, step = 100)
```

```{r}
#piping data from rarecurve into ggplot 
map_dfr(rareITS, bind_rows) %>%
  bind_cols(SampleID = rownames(OTUtabITS),.) %>%
  pivot_longer(-SampleID) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(n_seqs = as.numeric(str_replace(name, "N", ""))) %>%
  select(-name) %>%
 ggplot(aes(x=n_seqs, y=value, group=SampleID, color=SampleID)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=min_ITS_lib, color="gray") +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x="Sample Size", y="Species") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") 
ggsave("OriginalrareITSplot.pdf", width=8, height=5)
```

As we can see, this needs to be redone with the soil and the skin swab libraries separate. Time to rarefy soil samples:

```{r}
#to make the rarefaction curve, need to extract otu table 
taxa_are_rows(soilfung2)
soilitstab <- otu_table(soilfung2)
class(soilitstab) <- "matrix" # as.matrix() will do nothing
## you get a warning here, but this is what we need to have
soilitstab <- t(soilitstab) # transpose observations to rows
```

```{r}
soilitsrare <- rarecurve(soilitstab, step = 100)
```

```{r}
#piping data from rarecurve into ggplot 
map_dfr(soilitsrare, bind_rows) %>%
  bind_cols(SampleID = rownames(soilitstab),.) %>%
  pivot_longer(-SampleID) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(n_seqs = as.numeric(str_replace(name, "N", ""))) %>%
  select(-name) %>%
 ggplot(aes(x=n_seqs, y=value, group=SampleID, color=SampleID)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=min_ITS_lib2, color="gray") +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x="Sample Size", y="Species") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") 
ggsave("raresoilITSplot.pdf", width=8, height=5)
```

```{r}
# Initialize matrices to store richness and evenness estimates for all of the samples
soilITS <- subset_samples(soilfung, Stage != 'Void ')

nITSsamp = nsamples(soilITS)
ITStrials = 100

fungrichness <- matrix(nrow = nITSsamp, ncol = ITStrials)
row.names(fungrichness) <- sample_names(soilITS)

fungevenness <- matrix(nrow = nITSsamp, ncol = ITStrials)
row.names(fungevenness) <- sample_names(soilITS)

fungshanmeas <- matrix(nrow = nITSsamp, ncol = ITStrials)
row.names(fungshanmeas) <- sample_names(soilITS)

# It is always important to set a seed when you subsample so your result is replicable 
set.seed(4)

for (i in 1:100) {
  # Subsample
  ri <- rarefy_even_depth(soilITS, sample.size = min_ITS_lib2, verbose = FALSE, replace = TRUE)
  
  # Calculate richness
  richfung <- as.numeric(as.matrix(estimate_richness(ri, measures = "Observed")))
  fungrichness[ ,i] <- richfung
  
  # Calculate evenness
  evenfung <- as.numeric(as.matrix(estimate_richness(ri, measures = "InvSimpson")))
  fungevenness[ ,i] <- evenfung

  #calc Shannon
  Shannonfung <- as.numeric(as.matrix(estimate_richness(ri, measures = "Shannon")))
  fungshanmeas[ ,i] <- Shannonfung
}

# Create a new dataframe to hold the means and standard deviations of richness estimates
SampleID <- row.names(fungrichness)
mean <- apply(fungrichness, 1, mean)
sd <- apply(fungrichness, 1, sd)
measure <- rep("Richness", nITSsamp)
rich_stats_soilITS <- data.frame(SampleID, mean, sd, measure)

# Create a new dataframe to hold the means and standard deviations of evenness estimates
SampleID <- row.names(fungevenness)
mean <- apply(fungevenness, 1, mean)
sd <- apply(fungevenness, 1, sd)
measure <- rep("Inverse Simpson", nITSsamp)
even_stats_soilITS <- data.frame(SampleID, mean, sd, measure)

# Create a new dataframe to hold the means and standard deviations of evenness estimates
SampleID <- row.names(fungshanmeas)
mean <- apply(fungshanmeas, 1, mean)
sd <- apply(fungshanmeas, 1, sd)
measure <- rep("Shannon", nITSsamp)
shan_stats_soilITS <- data.frame(SampleID, mean, sd, measure)
```

```{r}
#Now we will combine our estimates for soil richness and evenness into one dataframe
soilITSalpha <- rbind(rich_stats_soilITS, even_stats_soilITS, shan_stats_soilITS)

#add metadata 

k <- data.frame(sample_data(soilITS))
colnames(k)[2] <- "SampleID"
adivsoilITS <- merge(soilITSalpha, k, by = "SampleID")
```

```{r}
#filter out the data for this test 
ObRichFSl <-filter(adivsoilITS,measure == "Richness")
ShannonFSl <-filter(adivsoilITS,measure == "Shannon")
InvSimpFSl <- filter(adivsoilITS,measure == "Inverse Simpson")
```

```{r}
ggsave("ITSObsSoilRichness.pdf", width=8, height=5)
```
